Policy rule R1: Verify before you block on a weak signal: R1. Verify before you block on a weak signal. If the case rests on a single signal (including a risk score alone) and your assessed fraud probability is below 0.70, recommend `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER` or `STEP_UP_AUTH` before any block. Blocking a legitimate customer on one signal is a policy breach.

Policy rule R6: Shared origin: R6. Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Monitoring sweep on card C00782-K1 over a $934.98 in person transaction on 2016-12-29 found the cardholder denied the transaction on contact. Two of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F, and the amount was 12.7x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. The card sits in a bounded component of 2 cards (C13355-K1) linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards, while the bank already has 1 confirmed-fraud case(s) closed on this card (CC-3048) with pattern(s): card_not_present_new_device. The 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one (CC-5502, CC-1192, CC-4870, CC-3722, CC-4562) closed as 5 confirmed fraud (account takeover, out of region use) and 0 cleared. The case was assessed as fraud at probability 0.94 with pattern account_takeover and exposure of $959.27, 1 other card(s) transacted through the same device profile in the window and are named for monitoring, and an external email-domain intelligence classification of 'gmail.com' carried no weight. Policy rule R2 recommended `BLOCK_CARD` and `CREATE_CASE`, and policy rule R6 recommended `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares the shared element.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-29 and 2016-12-31, card C00782-K1 belonging to customer C00782 was used for 2 transaction(s) totalling $959.27, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $934.98 on 2016-12-29, and this activity was conducted in person under product code W and billed in region 327.0. The cardholder denies the transaction on contact, and although the cardholder states they did not make the transaction and still holds the card, that response is an assumption recorded in the case file because no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. During this activity, 2 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on the $934.98 transaction, while the bank’s closed investigations already record 1 confirmed fraud case(s) on this card (CC-3579, CC-3048) with pattern(s) card_not_present_new_device. The same device profile was used by 1 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-12-29 (C13355-K1), and connected components over the device-sharing graph place this card in a bounded component of 2 cards (C13355-K1), linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards, indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder. This activity is suspicious because it is consistent with known fraud pattern 5, account takeover, which describes mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number, and the $934.98 amount is 12.7x this card’s median and above its 95th percentile. The bank also has 1 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-3048), and the 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one (CC-5502, CC-1192, CC-4870, CC-3722, CC-4562) closed as 5 confirmed fraud (account takeover, out of region use) and 0 cleared. The activity was assessed at a 94% probability of being fraudulent based on 4 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history, and it was reported because it connects to a device profile shared with other compromised cards, which requires a report regardless of amount. The total exposure is $959.27, the activity was first noticed between 2016-12-29 and 2016-12-31, and the card has been blocked and scheduled for reissue, an internal investigation case has been opened, and the cards sharing the same origin have been placed under monitoring.
